progress.text: · Inserting text with many returns no longer takes time that grows with their square (part of #1588): each return copied its paragraph's format with its own insert, moving every format after it. Splitting 20,000 returns into paragraphs took 15.8 s; placing a text file of them now takes 0.2 s, and one of a million returns 5.5 s. No readiness percentage change.

· Discretionary hyphens (U+00AD) break in the single-line composer with automatic hyphenation on or off, matching the paragraph composer. Unbroken soft hyphens remain invisible and zero-width, and words containing them keep only their discretionary break points (#1955). No readiness percentage change.

· Autoflow no longer sizes the rest of a story by a frame that a Start Paragraph option (next column, frame, page, or odd or even page) ends early (#1209). With a title before a chapter that starts on the next odd page, it estimated a page per few characters, added up to 2000 pages (the autoflow limit) and removed them again: placing 2000 words took 36 s in the app, now 0.4 s, with the same pages. It looks past tracked-deleted paragraphs for the option, as composing does, and asks for every frame that start options and breaks force in one round: 200 one-line chapters on their own pages take 9 ms (58 ms before). A break and the start option it meets count once, and breaks that tracked changes delete or a hidden condition hides don't count. No readiness percentage change.

· IDML export writes the document's default StoryPreference in Resources/Preferences.xml, as InDesign does. Only each story carried one, and IDML readers that take the spread reading order from the document's (Okapi's IDML filter) failed on DesignCraft's files. No readiness percentage change.

· An iconic panel's flyout stays open while you work in the canvas or a text field: Auto-Collapse Iconic Panels is off by default, and preferences saved with it on start with it off. Preferences › Interface › Panels holds the setting next to the column bar's menu item. No readiness percentage change.

· Inner Shadow, Inner Glow (from the edges) and Bevel and Emboss on a frame holding an image follow what the image paints: a transparent part is outside the object, so the effect lines the image's opaque edge, not the frame (#1622). Satin and a centred Inner Glow still follow the frame. No readiness percentage change.

· Column rules run from the top line's ascent to the bottom line's descent, as InDesign draws them, instead of from the top to the bottom of the columns, on screen, in PDF and in PowerPoint export. The top and bottom insets shorten the rule from those lines. Existing documents draw their column rules at the new length. No readiness percentage change.

· Panels dock through the suite's shared docking (craft-libs), and on desktop a floating panel opens in its own window that can leave the main window: keys pressed there run the main window's shortcuts, clipboard and tool keys, and the canvas paints no tool cursor while another of the app's windows has the pointer. The web build keeps floating panels in the page. No readiness percentage change.

· Story Options rejects malformed or nonexistent explicit story/frame IDs without changing the selected story, including an invalid frame alongside a valid story. Null targets remain absent; omitted targets still use the selection. No readiness percentage change.

· Text Frame Options explains that a custom baseline-grid increment must be a measure greater than zero when zero, a negative value or a non-measure is entered. Validation is unchanged. No readiness percentage change.

· Renaming a paragraph or character style, or moving it into a style group, keeps its Export Tagging under the new name, and undo puts it back under the old one. Deleting a tagged style drops its tagging and leaves the replacement style's own tagging as it was. No readiness percentage change.

· Quick Apply and the application bar's search leave out the interface commands that failed or reset a setting when chosen there: those that need a workspace, a command and shortcut, a menu item, a panel, a window edge, an app page, a recent file or a swatch they can't give them, a Contextual Task Bar place, and Interface Color Theme, UI Scaling, Reset Shortcuts, the flattener preset, Screen Mode and Zoom To, which without a value switched to the dark theme, set 100%, cleared every custom shortcut or the preset, or went to Normal mode or 100% zoom. Each stays in the menu, panel or dialog that gives it the value. No readiness percentage change.

· EPUB Export Options › Split Document, a dialog before File › Export EPUB… saves (document.epubSplit, stored with the document): off, a single paragraph style, or based on paragraph style export tags, with Paragraph Style Options › Export Tagging's Split Document flag marking those styles. A reflowable EPUB is one content file unless Split Document is on; the split before each top-level h1 from #791 is gone. A split before a list item or preformatted line no longer leaves an unclosed list or block in a content file. IDML import and export keep the setting and the flag, and Load Styles the flag. No readiness percentage change.

· Optical Margin Alignment and hanging punctuation apply to lines with a tab or a right indent tab, as both composers already measured them: the edge glyphs hang, and tab stops stay where they are. Such a line was set without the hang: a justified line that fit only because its period or closing quote hangs had its word spaces squeezed to make up for it, and text after a right indent tab stopped at the measure instead of hanging. No readiness percentage change.

· The Story Editor has InDesign's vertical depth ruler between the style column and the text, and View › Story Editor › Show/Hide Depth Ruler (view.storyEditorDepthRuler) shows or hides it in the Story Editor, remembered with the preferences. The ruler is marked in the document's vertical ruler units with how deep the story's text fills its frames, counted through its columns and threaded frames (lines set side by side, in the sub-columns of a split paragraph or on both sides of a wrap object, count once), and is shaded down to the overset point, where a red line now crosses the editor. No readiness percentage change.

· Split Note (note.split {story, id, at}, the Notes panel's Split Note button): as in InDesign, a note splits in two at the insertion point in its text. DesignCraft moves the text after it into a new note by the same author, anchored right after the first. No readiness percentage change.

· Type › Notes › Previous Note and Next Note (note.previous, note.next): as in InDesign, they move the insertion point from note to note in the story, putting the caret after the note's anchor. Each item is unavailable when no note lies in its direction in the story, or when the insertion point is in a table cell or a footnote. No readiness percentage change.

· Type › Notes › Convert to Note (note.convertFromText {author?}): as in InDesign, the selected text leaves the story and becomes the text of a new note, whose anchor takes its place; Convert Note to Text puts it back. DesignCraft refuses a selection in a table cell, or one that holds a note, footnote, endnote, anchored object, index marker, text anchor, cross-reference or table. No readiness percentage change.

· Story panel (Window › Type & Tables › Story): Optical Margin Alignment and its size for the stories of the text selection or the selected text frames, disabled without either; type.selectionAttrs reports them as storyOptions, null where the stories differ. The Paragraph panel menu has Ignore Optical Margin in place of the per-paragraph Optical Margin Alignment switch, which stays in type.para, and Paragraph Style Options › Indents and Spacing has Ignore Optical Margin (#947). No readiness percentage change.

· Optical Margin Alignment per story with a size (story.options {opticalMargin, opticalMarginSize}, off by default): when it is on, the story's paragraphs hang punctuation and letter edges by amounts set for that type size, except paragraphs with Ignore Optical Margin (ignoreOpticalMargin in type.para and paragraph styles). Table cells and footnotes don't take the story setting yet. When it is off, the per-paragraph switch still hangs at the text's own size. IDML imports and exports both (StoryPreference/@OpticalMarginAlignment, @OpticalMarginSize, IgnoreEdgeAlignment) (#947). No readiness percentage change.

· Text frames: a custom baseline grid's Relative To (Text Frame Options › Baseline Options, object.textFrameOptions {baselineGrid: {relativeTo}}, IDML BaselineFrameGridRelativeOption) measures the grid's start from the top of the page, the top margin, the top of the frame or its top inset. Text Frame Options had no custom baseline grid controls, imports dropped the setting and every frame grid started from the page top, so grid-aligned text in a frame measured from its own top sat on the wrong lines. No readiness percentage change.

· Paragraph Style Options › Indents and Spacing has an Align to Grid menu: None, All Lines or First Line Only. It shows the style's current setting. A First Line Only style could be set only in the CJK Grid Settings section, which shows only with CJK features on, or through commands. No readiness percentage change.

· A guide pulled out of a ruler keeps the resize cursor across it until it is dropped; the tool's cursor took over as soon as the pointer left the ruler, so the drag looked as if it had stopped. No readiness percentage change.

· Anchored text frames, such as marginal notes, compose where their host story places them: they align to the baseline grid at that position, and page-number markers and spine-relative alignment inside them read the host's page. They composed against a grid measured from their stored position and on no page, so a note set to Only Align First Line to Grid could sit a fraction of a line off the body text's grid line. No readiness percentage change.

· Tables: a gradient swatch in a cell fill draws as a gradient on the canvas and in PDF, in one gradient space for the whole table, so it runs across cells without restarting. Cells showed the gradient's first stop as a solid colour. No readiness percentage change.

· New documents start with Hyphenate Capitalized Words, Hyphenate Last Word and Hyphenate Across Column off in [Basic Paragraph], as in InDesign. Opened and imported files keep the values they carry. No readiness percentage change.

· The baseline grid's Relative To setting applies: with Top Margin, the grid starts at each page's own top margin in text composition, on the canvas and for snapping. It started at the page top, so grid-aligned text sat on the wrong lines and a page could fit one line fewer. No readiness percentage change.

· Custom-positioned anchored objects honour Relative to Spine (anchored.options {spineRelative}, IDML SpineRelative): the settings describe a left-hand page and mirror on a right-hand page, so marginal notes stay in the outside margin on both pages of a spread. On right-hand pages they took the left-hand placement and landed in the inside margin, across the spine or over the body text. No readiness percentage change.

· Text frames: a custom baseline grid (Text Frame Options › Baseline Options) from an IDML file sets lines from its start by its increment. The composer read the two values in the other order, so lines landed on the wrong grid. No readiness percentage change.

· designcraft-cli mcp takes --automation-read-root and --automation-write-root more than once, as the suite's other apps do (#1552): a path inside any root of its kind passes, and the roots' common parent, .. or a link out of them and the other kind's roots stay refused. No readiness percentage change.

· Layout › Go Back and Go Forward (Cmd+Page Up / Cmd+Page Down, Ctrl on Windows and Linux) retrace the jumps between pages (Go to Page, the page and spread commands, the Pages panel) as InDesign's do, returning to where the view was on each page at the current zoom; a new jump after going back drops the pages ahead, scrolling adds no entry, and pages deleted since are skipped. No readiness percentage change.

· Effects dialog: with Use Global Light on, the Angle field (and the Bevel and Emboss one) stays editable and shows the document's global light angle; a change there sets the global light for every effect that uses it, applied with the effects in one undo step (object.effects takes globalLight). Before, the field was greyed out and the angle couldn't be changed in the dialog. No readiness percentage change.

· File › File Info… edits the document's Document Title, Author, Description, Keywords, Copyright Notice and Copyright Info URL (file.info), and the document saves them. PDF export (PDF/X-4 and Print Booklet included) writes the title, author, description and keywords into the PDF's document information and XMP. EPUB export takes the title and author from File Info, and HTML export takes the title. A title or author given to the export replaces File Info's, and an empty Document Title leaves the document's name as the title. No readiness percentage change.

· Save and export dialogs (Save As, Save a Copy, Export PDF and the other exports, Package, libraries and books) start in the active document's folder once it has been saved, and for a document never saved in the folder of the last file saved or exported, remembered across sessions (#1653). A folder deleted since falls back to the system's choice. No readiness percentage change.

· Translations: a missing string shows in English and fails no test; cargo xtask i18n-report, run by cargo xtask ci, prints the missing strings per language. Tests keep duplicate-key and placeholder checks and the language mechanics (lookup, context captions, plural captions, right-to-left). No readiness percentage change.

· Show Hidden Characters marks table cells as InDesign does: every cell shows its own spaces, tabs and paragraph returns and an end-of-story # after its text (an empty cell shows just the #), and the table paragraph's ¶ sits after the table's bottom right corner. Cells showed no marks. No readiness percentage change.

· Tables: with the Type tool in a cell, Shift+Tab goes back a cell (it went on to the next one) and Esc toggles between the text and the cell, as in InDesign: the insertion point selects its cell, and selected cells select the text of the first one (table.toggleSelection). Esc left the table for the frame. No readiness percentage change.

· Type › Text Variables › Convert Variable to Text (variables.convertToText): the variable instances in the selected text, in a story, a table cell or a footnote, become plain text of the value each shows on its own page (a running header on page 3 becomes page 3's heading). variables.convertAllToText {name} does the same for every instance of one variable in the document, as the Text Variables dialog's Convert to Text button. The variable stays defined; one undo step. No readiness percentage change.

· Autoflow (Shift-click with the loaded text cursor, autoflow on Place, text.thread {autoflow}) fills the pages that follow before it adds any, as InDesign does: one frame per column on each following page, whatever else the page holds, then new pages at the end of the document. It inserted pages right after the story's last frame, in front of the document's own pages. Frames it set past the end of the text go again; a page the document had stays, and a page autoflow added only for such a frame goes with it. Smart Text Reflow of the primary text frame is unchanged. No readiness percentage change.

· Hyphenation Settings, as in InDesign: the Paragraph panel menu's Hyphenation… (app.hyphenationDialog) sets the selected paragraphs' Hyphenate, Words with at Least, After First, Before Last, Hyphen Limit, Hyphenation Zone, the Better Spacing ↔ Fewer Hyphens slider (InDesign's 0–10 steps), Hyphenate Capitalized Words, Last Word and Across Column, with Preview, as one undo step; Paragraph Style Options › Hyphenation has the same form. The panel menu lists its items in InDesign's order. Replicated from a hyphenation tutorial: the same text in Minion Pro breaks into the same lines as InDesign's with hyphenation on, off, and at Fewer Hyphens. No readiness percentage change.
